headline: Record revenue, profit, and EPS across the Integrated Firm
summary_short: Morgan Stanley reported record Q2 2026 net revenues of $21.3B (+27.1% y/y) and record diluted EPS of $3.46 (+62.4% y/y), with net income applicable to Morgan Stanley of $5.58B (+57.7% y/y) and ROTCE of 26.6%.
summary_long: Net revenues rose 27.1% y/y (+3.7% q/q) to a record $21.3B, led by Institutional Securities (+44% y/y to $11.0B) on record Equity net revenues (+69%) and Investment Banking (+58%), plus Wealth Management's record $8.9B on higher asset-management fees and net interest income. Pre-tax income climbed 59.0% y/y to $7.3B and net income applicable to MS rose 57.7% y/y to $5.58B, lifting diluted EPS 62.4% y/y to a record $3.46. ROTCE was 26.6% and the expense efficiency ratio improved to 65% from 71%. The Firm repurchased $1.5B of stock, raised its quarterly dividend 15c to $1.15/share, and reauthorized a $20B multi-year buyback program beginning Q3 2026. CET1 (Standardized) fell to 14.8% from 15.0% a year ago.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited 'exceptional results' across all three regions, record revenues over $21B and record EPS of $3.46, led by Equity/Investment Banking momentum and record Wealth Management net new assets of $148B crossing the $10 trillion total-client-assets milestone.

Institutional Securities revenue rose on record Equity net revenues (client engagement, favorable markets, strength in Asia) plus higher Investment Banking on completed M&A and higher IPO/follow-on issuance; Wealth Management set a record on higher asset-management fees and net interest income.
Higher net revenues across all three segments outpaced expense growth; the Firm's own expense efficiency ratio improved to 65% from 71% a year ago.
Not explained separately in the release beyond the pre-tax income drivers above; the effective tax rate ticked up to 23.1% from 22.7% a year ago.
EPS grew faster than net income because diluted share count fell 1.5% y/y on continued buybacks ($1.5B repurchased this quarter).
